India congratulates the French presidency and notes the Secretary-General's briefing. While we welcome the UK's condemnation of Russian atrocities and the US's intent to submit a draft resolution condemning the sham referendums, we must distinguish between current reports and established facts. The UN report confirms these exercises were held under active conflict and outside Ukraine's legal framework, yet we cannot verify the specific details of the US draft resolution before its submission.

India reiterates its earlier position that the global South feels the acute pain of surging costs and shortages. We strongly oppose any measures that further complicate the struggling global economy. While we provide humanitarian assistance to Ukraine and economic support to stressed neighbours, we urge an immediate cessation of hostilities and a return to dialogue.

Regarding accountability, India maintains its stance that violations of international law must be investigated objectively. We supported calls for an independent investigation into the Bucha incident and remain committed to ending impunity. However, we caution that politics should not provide cover to evade accountability.

The current dossier does not establish India's endorsement or a recorded vote on the US draft resolution. Its absence from this document does not prove no official position exists. India calls for a peaceful resolution that upholds the territorial integrity of all states without exacerbating global economic instability.<|im_end|>

The United Kingdom reaffirms its unwavering support for Ukraine's sovereignty, territorial integrity, and right to self-determination. We stand with the Ukrainian people in their fight for freedom, as their struggle is the world's fight for freedom.

Regarding the current agenda, the United Kingdom notes with deep concern the recent sham referendums conducted by de facto authorities in Russian-controlled territories. As reported by the United Nations, these exercises were held during active armed conflict, outside Ukraine's legal framework, and cannot be regarded as a genuine expression of the popular will. The United Kingdom unequivocally rejects any attempt to alter Ukraine's status by force.

The United Kingdom welcomes the United States' intention to submit a draft resolution condemning these referendums, calling for non-recognition of altered status, and obligating Russia to withdraw its troops. We fully endorse the principles set out in that draft. However, we must distinguish between the United States' proposed text and any recorded vote or formal endorsement by the Security Council. The absence of a vote in this dossier does not preclude the existence of an official position; it merely reflects the current procedural status of the draft.

The United Kingdom also recalls its earlier position that the global South is acutely feeling the pain of the conflict, which has led to surging costs and shortages of food grains, fertilizers, and fuel. We call on all Member States to avoid measures that further complicate the struggling global economy.

Finally, the United Kingdom reiterates that there can be no impunity for those committing atrocities. The Council must send an unambiguous message that politics should never provide cover to evade accountability. We remain committed to securing peace and justice for all.<|im_end|>
